title: John Malkovich returns to the spotlight with ‘Wild Horse Nine’
seoTitle: John Malkovich returns to spotlight with Wild Horse Nine
subtitle: Actor receives 13-minute standing ovation and enters the Oscar race
excerpt: John Malkovich stars in ‘Wild Horse Nine’, a Martin McDonagh film that won a 13-minute ovation in Venice and is already tipped for the Best Actor Oscar.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Actor John Malkovich returned to the spotlight following the world premiere of Wild Horse Nine at the Venice Film Festival, where the film received a 13-minute standing ovation. The immediate acclaim has propelled the production into the Oscar race, especially in the Best Actor category.

What happens in ‘Wild Horse Nine’

Irish director Martin McDonagh presents a spy thriller set in 1973, starring Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as CIA agents in Santiago, Chile. The characters plot a coup against President Salvador Allende, but the veteran agent, played by Malkovich, begins to question the assassinations committed in the name of the "great cause."

Why the film is generating controversy

According to the BBC, the work offers a direct critique of CIA interference in democracies, describing the agents as "efficient and happy, yet horribly unjust." This political stance, unprecedented in McDonagh's work, could divide the American public and attract the attention of Academy voters.

Press and public reaction

IndieWire reports that the first question at the press conference was whether Malkovich felt ready to win an Oscar. The actor responded humbly, highlighting the quality of the screenplay and direction. The same publication mentions that the premiere featured a standing ovation and that the film is already being tipped as a strong contender for the award.

Awards and expectations

Variety highlights that the 13-minute ovation in Venice was one of the festival's longest and that the film has already "stormed into the Oscar race." The combination of award-winning direction, acclaimed screenplay, and performances by Malkovich and Rockwell fuels expectations of nominations in the Best Actor, Best Picture, and Best Director categories.

Impact on the Brazilian audience

For viewers in Brazil, the premiere offers an opportunity to reflect on historical and current foreign interventions, in addition to following one of contemporary cinema's most peculiar actors in one of his finest performances. The film's release in Brazilian theaters could broaden the debate on international politics and art as a form of social critique.

With information from BBC, IndieWire, Variety.
